title: The Gullible Husband and the Tree of Whispers
summary: In a village near Baghdad lived a simple, credulous farmer named Abu Bakr, whose gullibility was legendary across the district: if someone told him that donkeys laid golden eggs...
full_text:
In a village near Baghdad lived a simple, credulous farmer named Abu Bakr, whose gullibility was legendary across the district: if someone told him that donkeys laid golden eggs, he would spend three days checking the stables with a basket.

One morning, two mischievous youths resolved to test his credulity to the uttermost. One climbed into the hollow trunk of an ancient hollow oak tree, while the other waited beside the road.

When Abu Bakr passed with his mule, the youth shouted: 'Halt, Abu Bakr! The ancient Tree of Whispers is speaking your name!'

From within the hollow trunk, a deep, ghostly voice echoed: 'O Abu Bakr! Listen to the voice of destiny! Climb onto the highest branch of this oak, tie your ears together with your woollen turban, and crow like a rooster three times, and a pot of gold shall rain down from the sky!'

Abu Bakr did not pause for a second’s reflection. He tied his mule, scrambled up the oak tree, tied his turban around his ears, flapped his elbows, and began crowing with all his might: 'Cock-a-doodle-doo!'

A crowd of villagers, returning from the market, gathered beneath the tree in utter astonishment, laughing until tears rolled down their cheeks!

The village elder walked up and called: 'Abu Bakr! Are you laying an egg, or has the midday sun boiled your wits?'

Abu Bakr looked down, saw the two laughing youths running away with his mule’s pack-saddle, and realized with burning shame that he had been made the fool of the district.

He climbed down from the tree, embraced the laughter of his neighbors, and resolved never again to believe voices from trees before consulting his own common sense.
moral: Gullibility that believes every absurd tale makes a man a laughingstock; test rumors with reason.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
